+================================================================================
+VUT-COMPARE: ARCHITECTURE
+================================================================================
+
+This document describes the internal organisation of the comparison engine. It
+is intended for contributors and maintainers. For an introduction to what the
+component does and how to call it from outside, see README.txt.
+
+
+OVERVIEW
+========
+
+The engine compares two text streams - 'subject' (test output) and 'nominal'
+(golden reference) - and produces either a boolean verdict ('is_equivalent')
+or a structured alignment of their content ('associate'). Both modes share
+the same front end, the same lexical interpretation, and the same notion of
+tolerance. They diverge only after the input has been carved into comparable
+chunks; from there, the equivalence path is fast-fail, and the association
+path is exhaustive.
+
+Conceptually the data flows through five stages:
+
+    raw text     PatternFinder       ChunkPipe         input_chunk_zip
+    -------- -> ---------------- -> -------------- -> ----------------- ->
+    .readline()  LineElement[]      InputChunk[]      (subject, nominal)
+                 per Line                             chunk pairs
+
+                              +---------- equivalence path ----------+
+                              |                                      |
+                              |  InputChunk.is_equivalent_to_nominal |
+                              |  -> bool                             |
+                              |                                      |
+                              +--------- association path -----------+
+                                                                     |
+                                                ChunkPair.from_input_chunks
+                                                -> ChunkPair (LinePair[])
+
+Subject and nominal flow through the first three stages independently and in
+parallel. They first meet in 'input_chunk_zip', which pairs them up by chunk
+position, and from there the path forks based on the requested mode.
+
+
+MODULE MAP
+==========
+
+The tree is REGION-MAJOR: region kinds are the OPEN axis (each a package
+under region/), the two faces (equivalence 'Judge' / associate 'Lawyer')
+are the CLOSED axis -- an interface contract each region package fulfills.
+
+    /region/                 Region-handler packages (one per region kind)
+        registry.py          THE registry: shebang name -> handler; grammar
+                             '##! <handler> [<param>|<param>=<value>]*',
+                             parameter resolution, loud RegionSyntaxError
+        /line_sequence/      The core-language region (ordered lines)
+            equivalence.py   Judge face: line-level fast-fail check
+            associate.py     Lawyer face: order-respecting alignment
+        /verbatim/           Byte-exact ordered region (no tolerance)
+        /ignore/             Contents-exempt region
+        /point_cloud/        n-dim points: coverage/pair matching within
+                             'limit', distance functions, constraint
+                             properties; safe expression evaluator
+                             (expression.py); shared decision core
+                             (core.py) feeds BOTH faces; fixed-radius
+                             grid index (spatial.py) for built-in metrics
+        /table/              columnar rows: positional / bag / key-matched;
+                             per-column ignore + relative numeric tolerance;
+                             shared decision core (core.py) feeds BOTH faces
+        /potpourri/          Unordered blocks
+            equivalence.py   Judge face: complete-matching verdict
+            associate.py     Lawyer face: best-effort alignment
+            best_match.py    Similarity pairing for the display
+            pairing.py       Strict (exact-equivalence) pairing driver
+            matching.py      Matching state machine (ultimates, feasibility)
+            potential_pair_db.py    Candidate pairs + analogy constraints
+            result.py        Solver result container
+            solver/
+                maximum_bipartite_matching.py    Augmenting-path matcher
+                csp_backtracking_mrv.py          MRV-heuristic CSP solver
+
+    /core/                   Shared association machinery
+        chunk_pair.py        ChunkPair: outer container of LinePairs
+        line_pair.py         LinePair: aligned (or one-sided) line pair
+        edit_operations/     Edit-distance machinery
+            core.py          Work-list search base classes
+            line.py          Line-level edits over LineElement sequences
+            line_sequence.py Sequence-level edits over Line lists
+            string.py        Levenshtein for raw character runs
+            edit.py          Edit primitives, EditSequence
+            separator_adaptor.py  Strip/reinsert separators around a search
+
+    /engine/                 Shared substrate
+        semantics.py         THE single source of comparison semantics:
+                             edit classes, cost tables, verdict reductions,
+                             insignificance, analogy commit protocol
+                             (see DOC/SEMANTICS.txt)
+        enums.py             E_Verdict, E_Chunk, E_ToleranceId
+        line.py              Line as a sequence of LineElements
+        analogy_db.py        Mutable bidirectional analogy mapping
+        frozen_analogy_db.py Flyweight immutable variant for hot paths
+        constraints.py       Stateful constraints: '((name: value))'
+                             bindings feed a per-run constraint space;
+                             check-on-entry against Configuration.
+                             constraint_db (AST-whitelisted expressions);
+                             ContextVar-threaded like the flyweight
+                             registry (see DOC/SEMANTICS.txt sec. 10)
+        /input/              Lexical and structural front end
+            line_element.py  Atomic units of comparison (one per token type)
+            pattern_finder.py Regex master pattern; text -> LineElement[]
+            line_scanner.py  THE raw-line classification (region begin/
+                             end, blank, ignored, content) shared by both
+                             pipes; '##!'/'####' precedence over '##'
+            input_chunk.py   LineSequence / Potpourri / Line containers
+            chunk_pipe.py    async producer: line stream -> InputChunk stream
+            input_chunk_zip.py async pairer: subject + nominal -> chunk pairs
+
+    /feeder/                 Output adaptors
+        ui.py                ChunkPair stream -> DisplayInst protocol
+        html_feeder.py       Side-by-side HTML diff renderer
+
+    /tool/                   Maintenance utilities
+        migrate_region_syntax.py   one-shot '||||' -> shebang migration
+
+    main.py                  Public API: is_equivalent(), associate(),
+                             is_equivalent_by_association (reference Judge);
+                             cross-check mode (VUT_COMPARE_CROSS_CHECK=1)
+    configuration.py         Configuration dataclass
+
+
+DATA TYPES
+==========
+
+LineElement (engine/input/line_element.py)
+    The atomic unit of comparison. Each LineElement carries a tolerance class
+    (STRING, NUMERIC, ANALOGY, VISIBLE_NOTHING, EQUIVALENCE_PATTERN, SEPARATOR)
+    and the matched content. Tolerance dictates how '.compare()' decides
+    equivalence:
+      STRING               byte-equal
+      NUMERIC              equal within configured epsilon
+      ANALOGY              consistent under the active analogy database
+      VISIBLE_NOTHING      always equivalent (transparent token)
+      EQUIVALENCE_PATTERN  same pattern set
+      SEPARATOR            structural marker, byte-equal
+    Strings are interned via 'sys.intern()'; '__slots__' is used throughout
+    for memory; this class is allocated millions of times in large runs.
+
+Line (engine/line.py)
+    Sequence of LineElements representing one source line, plus the line
+    number. Caches its lexical decomposition lazily. Exposes:
+      .is_literally_equivalent_to(other)    fast byte-level shortcut
+      .is_equivalent(other, analogy_db)     full equivalence under analogies
+      .edit_operations(other, analogy_db)   produces an EditSequence
+      .compare_quickly(other)               cheap structural similarity score
+
+InputChunk (engine/input/input_chunk.py)
+    A region of one stream classified by structure:
+      InputChunkLine          single line (used in equivalence mode)
+      InputChunkLineSequence  ordered group of lines (used in association mode)
+      InputChunkPotpourri     unordered region ('##! potpourri' .. '####')
+      InputChunkVerbatim      byte-exact region  ('##! verbatim'  .. '####')
+      InputChunkIgnore        contents-exempt region ('##! ignore' .. '####')
+      InputChunkPointCloud    n-dim point region  ('##! point-cloud' .. '####')
+      InputChunkTable         columnar region     ('##! table' .. '####')
+      InputChunkTerminal      end-of-stream sentinel
+      InputChunkVoid          padding for the zip stage
+    Two role-tagged base classes split the contract:
+      EquivalenceRelatedInputChunk.is_equivalent_to_nominal()
+      AssociationRelatedInputChunk.associate_with_nominal()
+    Concrete chunks may inherit one or both depending on whether the chunk
+    type is meaningful in that mode (e.g. Potpourri inherits both, Line
+    inherits only equivalence).
+
+ChunkPair (core/chunk_pair.py)
+    The output unit of association: a list of LinePairs plus a snapshot of
+    the analogy_db that holds for them. A ChunkPair carries the chunk-type
+    tags of both sides; if subject or nominal is missing, the corresponding
+    type is NONE. The 'feeder' subsystem consumes ChunkPair streams.
+
+LinePair (core/line_pair.py)
+    One row of the alignment: a subject line, a nominal line, optionally
+    None on either side, plus the cell-level edit results showing how
+    individual LineElements were aligned. Carries its own equivalence
+    reduction ('.is_equivalent()', derived from semantics.GOOD_EDIT_ID_SET)
+    -- the Lawyer's side of THE LAW (see DOC/SEMANTICS.txt).
+
+AnalogyDb / FrozenAnalogyDb (engine/analogy_db.py, frozen_analogy_db.py)
+    Bidirectional mapping between subject-side and nominal-side analogy
+    strings. AnalogyDb is mutable and used during top-level streaming;
+    FrozenAnalogyDb is immutable, interned, and used inside the inner
+    search loops where consistency checks happen millions of times.
+
+
+THE TWO PIPELINES
+=================
+
+Both modes share the lexer ('PatternFinder'), the line representation
+('Line'), and the chunking strategy. They differ in three places:
+
+   stage                  equivalence mode             association mode
+   --------------------   --------------------------   --------------------------
+   ChunkPipe              EquivalenceCheckChunkPipe    AssociationChunkPipe
+                          emits InputChunkLine per     emits InputChunkLineSequence
+                          line; DROPS insignificant    blocks; KEEPS every line
+                          lines and whole-line         for display
+                          visible-nothing (both pipes
+                          classify via the shared
+                          engine/input/line_scanner)
+   chunk_zip              generate_chunk_pairs         generate_chunk_pairs_type_aligned
+                          one-shot pair-and-yield      look-ahead realignment when
+                                                       subject and nominal chunk
+                                                       types diverge
+   per-chunk operation    InputChunk.is_equivalent_    ChunkPair.from_input_chunks
+                          to_nominal -> bool           -> ChunkPair (full alignment)
+
+The async producer/consumer arrangement is identical in both: each ChunkPipe
+runs in its own asyncio task, pushing into a bounded queue; the zip
+coroutine pulls from both queues with 'asyncio.gather'. This means subject
+data can be consumed while the test process is still producing it.
+
+
+KEY ALGORITHMS
+==============
+
+Edit-distance search (core/edit_operations/)
+    A work-list search over the (si, ni) index space, where si and ni are
+    indices into the subject and nominal LineElement sequences. From any
+    position, six-or-so edit operations are possible (GOOD, GOOD_TOLERATED,
+    GOOD_INSERT/DELETE, TRANSPOSE, SUBSTITUTE, SUBSTITUTE_TYPE, INSERT,
+    DELETE), each with a cost; the optimal edit sequence is the cheapest
+    path from (0, 0) to (len(subject), len(nominal)). The search uses
+    aggressive pruning: better-than-current-best work items are kept;
+    stale ones are dropped early. The same pattern is reused at the
+    line-sequence level - same machinery, different element type.
+
+    The 'string.py' Levenshtein implementation handles the leaf case where
+    two STRING-class elements need their character-level distance.
+
+    'do()' for line-level edits is wrapped in lru_cache: many Lines repeat
+    in large tests, and recomputing their edit sequence is wasteful.
+
+Bipartite matching (region/potpourri/solver/maximum_bipartite_matching.py)
+    For Potpourri chunks the order is irrelevant; the question is whether
+    a complete subject-to-nominal pairing exists. The solver uses Berge's
+    augmenting-path algorithm (Ford-Fulkerson family) to find the maximum
+    matching ignoring analogy constraints. This is the structural upper
+    bound: if it cannot find a complete matching, no analogy-respecting
+    matching exists either.
+
+CSP backtracking with MRV (region/potpourri/solver/csp_backtracking_mrv.py)
+    Once structural feasibility is confirmed, the actual matching that
+    satisfies analogy consistency is found by backtracking search ordered
+    by Minimum Remaining Values - the most-constrained subject is matched
+    first. This is the workhorse for Potpourri association in production;
+    other solvers (chronological backtracking, AC-3 / lilly-pad) are
+    retained in the source tree for benchmarking but are not active.
+
+Fixed-radius grid index (region/point_cloud/spatial.py)
+    The point-cloud queries are fixed-radius ("who is within 'limit'?"),
+    never k-nearest -- so a uniform grid with cell edge = limit beats
+    tree structures: any within-limit neighbour lies in one of the 3^d
+    adjacent cells (L-inf <= L1, L2). Build O(n), query O(1) expected,
+    exact, deterministic; used for built-in metrics with dimension <= 6.
+    Expression metrics carry no guaranteed triangle inequality and are
+    therefore scanned exactly (nothing may prune them).
+
+Flyweight FrozenAnalogyDb (engine/frozen_analogy_db.py)
+    The hottest inner-loop operation is "given two analogy databases, are
+    they consistent with each other?". Naive implementations rebuild the
+    bidict and compare; FrozenAnalogyDb interns each (subject, nominal)
+    pair into a small integer ID via a per-context registry, and represents
+    the active pair set as a 256-bit mask when the ID range allows. Two
+    identical constraint sets land at the same memory address, reducing
+    consistency checks to identity comparisons. For larger sets the
+    bitmask is replaced by a tuple of pair IDs; correctness is preserved
+    at the cost of slower checks, hence the term "Hybrid".
+
+    The registry is held in a 'contextvars.ContextVar', which means that
+    concurrent 'is_equivalent' or 'associate' calls in different asyncio
+    tasks see independent registries. This avoids cross-test poisoning
+    and lets the comparison engine be used safely from multiple coroutines
+    in the same process.
+
+
+ASYNC AND CONCURRENCY MODEL
+===========================
+
+Every pipeline stage is async by design. The 'main' entry points
+('is_equivalent', 'associate') are coroutines that:
+
+  1. Set a fresh FrozenAnalogyRegistry on the contextvar (isolation).
+  2. Wrap each line provider in 'AsyncIterator_ensured' so that both
+     synchronous file objects and async readers work uniformly.
+  3. Construct the per-mode ChunkPipe for each side.
+  4. Iterate over the chunk-pair generator, applying the per-mode logic
+     to each pair.
+  5. Reset the contextvar in a 'finally' clause - mandatory for isolation.
+
+The chunk_zip layer enforces backpressure through bounded asyncio.Queues.
+Subject and nominal pipelines run concurrently; if the consumer is slow,
+the queues fill and the producers wait. If subject is being produced live
+by a test process, the comparison can run in parallel and abort the test
+as soon as 'is_equivalent' returns False.
+
+The cancellation pattern is standard: on exception or normal completion,
+the producer tasks are cancelled and gathered with 'return_exceptions=True'.
+There are no shared mutable structures across coroutines outside the
+contextvar registry.
+
+
+VERDICT MODEL
+=============
+
+The leaf comparison operation is 'LineElement.compare(other) -> E_Verdict'.
+The verdict carries five values:
+
+    MISFIT         the two elements are of incomparable kinds
+    DIFFERENT      same kind, content does not agree
+    EQUIVALENT     same kind, content agrees (possibly under analogies)
+    EQUIVALENT_SUBJECT_VISIBLE_NOTHING   subject is transparent
+    EQUIVALENT_NOMINAL_VISIBLE_NOTHING   nominal is transparent
+
+The two VISIBLE_NOTHING variants are propagated rather than collapsed to
+EQUIVALENT so that downstream stages can account for "noise lines" without
+losing the information that the lines were transparent. Higher levels
+(Line, InputChunk) reduce these to plain booleans only at the end.
+
+
+TESTING CONVENTIONS
+===================
+
+This component is itself tested under HWUT (the older generation), with
+test files at multiple levels:
+
+    TEST/                        whole-engine tests via main.py API
+                                 (incl. test-consistency-fuzz.py, the
+                                 generative Judge/Lawyer consistency net)
+    engine/TEST/                 engine-internal contract tests
+    region/potpourri/TEST/       potpourri-specific scenarios
+    region/potpourri/solver/TEST/  solver micro-benchmarks
+    feeder/TEST/                 output formatting tests
+    engine/input/TEST/           pattern_finder, chunk_pipe tests
+
+Each test directory has the standard HWUT layout: 'hwut-info.dat' lists
+test files and exclusions; each '<test>.py' responds to '--hwut-info' with
+its CHOICES; outputs go to 'OUT/' and are compared against 'GOOD/'.
+
+Notable test patterns:
+  - regression-1 / 2 / 3        scenario-based regression suites
+  - test-*-race.py              async timing scenarios with jitter injection
+  - benchmark.py                non-test performance probes
+
+Coverage is collected with 'coverage run' as configured in 'hwut-info.dat'.
+Helpers ('common.py', 'racing.py', 'tmp.py', 'benchmark*.py') are excluded
+from both test runs and coverage.
+
+
+EXTENSION POINTS
+================
+
+New tolerance class
+    Add an entry to E_ToleranceId, a LineElement subclass with its own
+    .compare() and .edit_distance_relative(), and a regex pattern in
+    PatternFinder. The new class participates automatically in the rest
+    of the pipeline.
+
+New region kind
+    Create a package under region/ providing the chunk class with the two
+    faces -- '_is_equivalent_to_nominal' (Judge) and
+    '_associate_with_nominal' (Lawyer) -- which must satisfy THE LAW and
+    the region-handler contract (no analogy state in or out; substrate
+    rules untouched; see DOC/SEMANTICS.txt section 7). Then ONE
+    registration in region/registry.py (name, chunk class, parameter
+    spec) plus an E_Chunk display tag. Acceptance gate: full corpus +
+    fuzz net under VUT_COMPARE_CROSS_CHECK=1. 'verbatim' and 'ignore'
+    are the reference examples.
+
+New solver
+    Place under region/potpourri/solver/. Solvers consume a
+    'PotentialPairDb' and an 'AnalogyDb' and return either a
+    matching-or-None or a verdict-plus-couples pair, depending on the
+    expected interface. The active solver choice is wired in
+    region/potpourri/matching.py.
+
+New output feeder
+    Subscribe to the 'associate' coroutine output (an async iterator of
+    ChunkPair). 'feeder/ui.py' is the canonical example - see the protocol
+    signature mechanism it uses to declare structural compatibility with
+    a UI consumer.
+
+

+================================================================================
+VUT-COMPARE: COMPARISON SEMANTICS
+================================================================================
+
+This document is the AUTHORITATIVE description of what the comparison engine
+considers equivalent and why. It is the source from which the user manual's
+comparison chapter is to be written, and the reference against which the
+implementation is audited. Where code and this document disagree, one of the
+two has a bug -- file it.
+
+Section 10 is a decision log: every semantic ruling, its date, its rationale,
+and where it is implemented and verified.
+
+ARCHITECTURE.txt describes HOW the engine is built; this document describes
+WHAT the engine means.
+
+
+1. THE TWO FACES AND THE LAW
+============================
+
+The engine answers the same question in two ways:
+
+    is_equivalent(subject, nominal)    the JUDGE -- a fast-fail boolean.
+    associate(subject, nominal)        the LAWYER -- a full alignment of
+                                       both streams, for diff display.
+
+THE LAW (the engine's central invariant):
+
+    is_equivalent(subject, nominal) is True
+        <=>  associate(subject, nominal) yields only equivalent pairs
+             (ChunkPair.is_equivalent() for every chunk).
+
+The Judge is an optimization of the Lawyer, never an independent authority.
+What the user sees in the diff display and what the boolean verdict says can
+never disagree; any divergence is a bug by definition.
+
+The LAW is machine-checkable. With the environment variable
+
+    VUT_COMPARE_CROSS_CHECK=1        (or Configuration.cross_check_f)
+
+every 'is_equivalent' call additionally derives the verdict through the
+Lawyer ('is_equivalent_by_association') and raises 'CrossCheckError' with
+the complete input on divergence. The mode is off by default and free when
+off. It buffers both streams up-front, so the fast path's early-abort
+economy is suspended under the flag; tests that instrument stream reading
+(consumption logs, registry spies) are meaningful without the flag only.
+
+
+2. LINE CLASSIFICATION
+======================
+
+Every raw input line is classified ONCE, by 'engine/input/line_scanner.py',
+identically for both faces:
+
+    REGION_BEGIN       region opening: '##! <handler> <params...>'.
+    REGION_END         region closing: the line '####', EXACTLY. A run of
+                       five or more '#' is NOT a region end -- it stays an
+                       IGNORED commentary bar.
+    BLANK              only whitespace.
+    IGNORED            carries the ignored-line markers: the stripped line
+                       begins with '##' or ends with '##' (configurable).
+    CONTENT            everything else -- subject to comparison.
+
+Precedence is fixed and load-bearing: REGION_BEGIN before REGION_END before
+BLANK before IGNORED before CONTENT. A region marker must never be
+swallowed by the generic ignored-line rule -- the shebang framing '##!'
+itself begins with the ignored marker '##'.
+
+BLANK and IGNORED together are the INSIGNIFICANT lines -- "the Judge does
+not see this line". The single definition is
+'semantics.is_insignificant_line'; the scanner refines it into two classes
+without ever disagreeing with it. The two faces treat insignificance
+differently but CONSISTENTLY:
+
+    Judge    drops insignificant lines entirely; they can neither match
+             nor mismatch anything.
+    Lawyer   keeps them for display; in the alignment they appear as
+             one-sided filler pairs which are NEUTRAL for equivalence
+             (LinePair.is_equivalent() returns True for pairs made purely
+             of insignificant lines).
+
+Consequence for test authors: '##'-marked commentary and blank lines may be
+added, removed, or reordered freely without affecting any verdict.
+
+
+3. TOLERANCE CLASSES
+====================
+
+Inside a CONTENT line, the lexer decomposes text into 'LineElement's, each
+with a tolerance class that defines its notion of "equal":
+
+    STRING               byte-equal.
+    NUMERIC              equal within the configured relative tolerance
+                         ('numeric_tolerance_ratio'; 0 = exact). The band
+                         is centred on the NOMINAL, the 'pole'; its radius
+                         is 'abs(nominal) * ratio' -- a radius carries no
+                         sign (D-27).
+    ANALOGY              '((...))'-wrapped placeholder; equal under a
+                         consistent analogy binding (section 5).
+    EQUIVALENCE_PATTERN  words declared mutually equivalent (e.g.
+                         'happy' ~ 'glad'); equal iff both sides match the
+                         same pattern set.
+    VISIBLE_NOTHING      a token that means "nothing" (e.g. 'nothing',
+                         'nix'); see section 4.
+    SEPARATOR            whitespace runs; equal as structure, tolerated in
+                         width when whitespace tolerance is on.
+
+A line whose text is insignificant (section 2) lexes into a single
+VISIBLE_NOTHING element covering the whole line. (Edge, documented: this
+lexer-level judgment assumes 'strip_whitespace_f=True', the default; with
+stripping disabled, indented or trailing-marker lines are classified
+insignificant by the pipes but lexed as content -- an untested
+configuration, see decision log D-14.)
+
+
+4. VISIBLE NOTHING
+==================
+
+A VISIBLE_NOTHING token is printable text that counts as NOTHING for the
+comparison. Two rules, deliberately different in scope:
+
+WHOLE-LINE RULE (line sequences): a line consisting exclusively of
+VISIBLE_NOTHING elements equals NO LINE AT ALL. The single definition is
+'Line.is_visible_nothing'. The Judge's pipe skips such lines in sequence
+context; the Lawyer's sequence search classifies them GOOD_INSERT /
+GOOD_DELETE (equivalence-preserving skips). Hence:
+
+    subject:  alpha            nominal:  alpha
+              nothing                    beta
+              beta
+                               =>  EQUIVALENT.
+
+POTPOURRI EXCEPTION: inside a potpourri region, VN-only lines are COUNTED
+like any other line (both faces). A potpourri with an extra 'nothing' line
+is NOT equivalent to one without it.
+
+IN-LINE LIMIT: a VISIBLE_NOTHING token INSIDE a line does not make its
+surrounding separators disappear. 'alpha nothing beta' is NOT equivalent
+to 'alpha beta': after removing the token, the first line still carries
+two separator runs where the second has one. Both faces agree (cross-check
+verified). Widening this would be a deliberate feature change requiring
+matched edits on both faces (decision log D-10).
+
+
+5. ANALOGY SEMANTICS
+====================
+
+An analogy '((X))' is a placeholder: the subject may print a different
+token than the nominal recorded, as long as the correspondence is
+CONSISTENT. If '((B))' appears in the subject where '((A))' appears in the
+nominal, then B is the representative of A; the binding is one-to-one in
+both directions (a bidict): B cannot also stand for something else, and
+nothing else can stand for A.
+
+5.1 The global analogy db -- sequential, outer scope
+----------------------------------------------------
+
+The global analogy db belongs to the OUTER text (the line sequences between
+regions). It develops SEQUENTIALLY over the complete run, in stream order:
+the first occurrence establishes the binding; every later outer occurrence
+must honor it, or the streams are not equivalent. There is no lookahead and
+no solving across the stream -- a later line cannot retroactively change an
+established binding.
+
+    subject:  x ((B))          nominal:  x ((A))     -> binds B = A
+              ((B))                      ((B))       -> B already stands
+                                                        for A; NOT
+                                                        equivalent.
+
+Canonical key form: bindings are stored under the full marker-wrapped
+string ('((B))', never bare 'B') -- one vocabulary for every commit path
+('PatternFinder.extract_analogy_strings' is the single source). A second
+vocabulary would fragment consistency checking silently (this was a real
+bug; decision log D-12).
+
+5.2 Region-local isolation
+--------------------------
+
+EVERY REGION HAS ITS OWN ANALOGY DB. The global db is not propagated into
+a region, and a region's local frame is not propagated out. The global db
+develops over the complete run independent of any region's local frame.
+
+Consequences, all deliberate:
+
+  - A binding established in the outer text does NOT constrain how a
+    potpourri matches its lines, and vice versa. There is NO leakage in
+    either direction.
+  - Two regions are independent of each other: '((B))' may stand for
+    '((A))' inside one region and for '((B))' inside the next.
+  - Region-internal ambiguity can never poison any verdict outside the
+    region.
+
+5.3 Intra-region matching -- CSP with backtracking
+--------------------------------------------------
+
+Within one potpourri, lines pair by full constraint search: the region is
+equivalent iff a complete subject-to-nominal matching exists under an
+internally consistent local frame (starting empty). The CSP backtracks
+freely -- if an early pairing choice makes a later line unmatchable, the
+solver revises it. Crossed frames (B standing for A while A stands for B)
+are legal and found whenever the region's content forces them.
+
+TIE RULE: when several complete matchings are equally valid, the
+LEAST-COMMITTAL one is chosen deterministically -- a symbol stands for
+itself whenever it can ('semantics.analogy_commitment' orders candidates;
+remaining ties break by lowest nominal line number). This replaces
+hash-order luck; it does not prune the search. Since regions are isolated
+(5.2), the choice only determines the DISPLAYED pairing, never a verdict
+outside the region.
+
+LUCKY DAY: if a tie binds ((B))=((A)) locally and neither symbol recurs,
+any choice was fine. This is deliberately unproblematic.
+
+
+6. EQUIVALENCE IS EDIT-CLASS MEMBERSHIP, NEVER A COST TEST
+==========================================================
+
+The Lawyer's alignment assigns every edit an edit class; the classes that
+PRESERVE equivalence are exactly the GOOD family:
+
+    GOOD             byte-equal match
+    GOOD_TOLERATED   match under tolerance (numeric, analogy, pattern,
+                     whitespace)
+    GOOD_INSERT      visible-nothing appears on the nominal side only
+    GOOD_DELETE      visible-nothing appears on the subject side only
+
+('semantics.GOOD_EDIT_ID_SET' / 'is_good_edit()' -- the single source.)
+
+Costs exist ONLY to rank alternative alignments; they are never the
+equivalence criterion. The two deliberately disagree in the margins:
+
+  - a visible-nothing skip costs 1e-10 (so a plain GOOD wins when both
+    exist) yet PRESERVES equivalence;
+  - a separator INSERT/DELETE can cost 0 after separator normalization
+    yet BREAKS equivalence;
+  - a one-sided line pair carries cost 0.0 yet is not equivalent.
+
+The display's cell relations (OK_*/BAD_*) are derived mechanically from
+the edit classes, so "green in the display" and "counts as equal" cannot
+drift apart.
+
+
+7. REGIONS
+==========
+
+A region declares its own interpretation through a shebang line:
+
+    ##! <handler> [<param> | <param>=<value>]*
+    ...region lines...
+    ####
+
+The registry ('region/registry.py') maps the handler name to its
+implementation -- the OPEN axis: a new region kind is a new package under
+region/ plus one registration, no shared machinery is touched.
+
+7.1 Framing rules (all violations are LOUD RegionSyntaxErrors with line
+    numbers -- an input that looks like a region declaration is never
+    silently degraded to content):
+
+  - unknown handler name; unknown or malformed parameter;
+  - '##!' inside an open region (nesting is forbidden);
+  - '####' outside any region;
+  - end of stream inside an open region ('####' missing).
+
+7.2 Framing must MATCH between subject and nominal: a region on one side
+with no region (or a different handler) on the other is NOT equivalent --
+EVEN IF THE REGION IS EMPTY. Only a handler's contents are governed by the
+handler; the framing is structural.
+
+7.3 Parameters resolve with precedence: shebang parameter > handler-scoped
+configuration section (Configuration.region['<handler>']) > the handler's
+spec default. Example: '##! potpourri max_comparisons=64'. A BRACED value
+'{...}' may contain whitespace (expression parameters):
+'constraint={abs(y - sin(x)/x) < 0.01}'.
+
+NOMINAL IS AUTHORITATIVE: the comparison semantics are governed by the
+NOMINAL side's resolved parameters. The subject's shebang need only name
+the same handler; its parameters are syntax-checked but never applied --
+and expression parameters from the subject are NEVER evaluated (the
+subject is untrusted test output).
+
+7.4 The REGION-HANDLER CONTRACT:
+
+  - a handler receives the region's lines of both streams and returns the
+    equivalence verdict (Judge face) or the line alignment (Lawyer face);
+  - both faces of one handler must satisfy THE LAW (section 1) -- the
+    cross-check over corpus and fuzz net is the acceptance gate;
+  - a handler receives NO analogy state and exports NONE (section 5.2);
+  - insignificant-line handling and lexing come from the shared substrate
+    (sections 2, 3) -- a handler governs how CONTENT lines compare, never
+    which lines take part.
+
+7.5 Built-in handlers:
+
+POTPOURRI: the same lines must occur on both sides, in ANY order.
+Precisely: analogy-carrying lines and non-analogy lines are counted
+separately and must agree in number (VN-only lines included, section 4);
+non-analogy lines must admit a perfect matching of equivalent lines
+(maximum bipartite matching); analogy lines must admit a complete matching
+under a consistent local frame (CSP, section 5.3).
+Parameters (nominal-authoritative):
+    max_comparisons=<int>  complexity cap of the similarity pairing
+                           (default 128).
+    subset (flag)          only the SUBJECT lines must each find a
+                           DISTINCT equivalent partner; surplus nominal
+                           lines are legal (subject-as-subset-of-nominal),
+                           shown neutrally in the display.
+    duplicates (flag)      repeated lines COLLAPSE before matching (set
+                           semantics). Collapse is LITERAL -- by the
+                           whitespace-normalized uniform string; two lines
+                           that are merely tolerantly-equal do NOT
+                           collapse. Collapsed repetitions are display-
+                           neutral. Combines with subset.
+
+VERBATIM: byte-exact, ordered. NO tolerance of any kind applies to content
+lines -- no numeric epsilon, no analogies, no visible-nothing, no
+equivalence patterns, no whitespace normalization; line counts and order
+must agree. Blank and '##'-marked lines REMAIN insignificant (contract
+7.4: the handler does not redefine which lines take part).
+
+IGNORE: contents are exempt from judgment -- any content, any count, on
+either side. The framing itself must still match (7.2).
+
+POINT-CLOUD: every line is one point p[] in n dimensions (whitespace-
+separated floats; the region's first valid point sets the dimension).
+Parameters (nominal-authoritative; at least one of limit/constraint):
+
+    limit=<float>       distance criterion. Default mode: SYMMETRIC
+                        COVERAGE -- every point of either stream has a
+                        nearest neighbour in the other at distance <=
+                        limit (counts free, duplicates collapse). With
+                        'pair': a BIJECTIVE matching must exist with all
+                        pairs <= limit (equal counts; each point pairs
+                        exactly once; maximum-bipartite-matching decides).
+    dist=<spec>         'euclidean' (default), 'L1', 'L2', 'Linf', or an
+                        expression over x[] and y[].
+    constraint={expr}   property every point of BOTH streams must satisfy;
+                        over p[] with aliases x,y,z,w = p[0..3]. Alone
+                        (without limit): pure property check, counts
+                        irrelevant -- the GOOD file acts as a
+                        SPECIFICATION, not a recording.
+
+PERFORMANCE (internal, semantics-neutral): for built-in metrics the
+fixed-radius queries run over a uniform grid with cell edge = limit
+(candidates = the 3^d adjacent cells; results byte-identical to the
+brute-force scan, verified by a grid-vs-brute property family in the
+test). Expression metrics have no guaranteed triangle inequality, so
+nothing may prune them -- they use the exact O(n*m) scan.
+
+TABLE: every line is a row of columns (0-based). Cells split on whitespace,
+or on a literal 'sep={<string>}'. Parameters (nominal-authoritative; the
+nominal's first row sets the column count):
+
+    key=<col>          rows matched by equality of this column (implies
+                       unordered). Duplicate keys in the NOMINAL are a
+                       broken specification (loud).
+    ignore=<cols>      comma-separated column indices excluded from the
+                       comparison (timestamps, PIDs, ...).
+    numeric={c:t,...}  per-column RELATIVE numeric tolerance:
+                       |s - n| <= t * |n|.
+    unordered (flag)   rows form a bag: a bijective matching of rule-equal
+                       rows must exist (maximum bipartite matching).
+    sep={<string>}     split cells on a literal separator (cells stripped).
+
+Without key/unordered rows compare positionally and counts must agree.
+Malformed data is asymmetric (7.4 spirit): nominal defects (inconsistent
+column count, out-of-range column reference, unparsable numeric cell,
+duplicate key) are broken specifications -> loud RegionSyntaxError; the
+same defects on the subject side are test failures -> not equivalent,
+shown red.
+
+Expressions are SAFE: parsed and validated against a strict AST whitelist
+(vectors, arithmetic, comparisons, boolean ops, fixed math functions);
+anything else is rejected loudly at parse time; raw eval never runs on
+input text ('region/point_cloud/expression.py'). Malformed data is
+ASYMMETRIC: nominal defects (non-point line, dimension clash, data
+violating its own constraint) are broken specifications -> loud error;
+the same defects on the subject side are test failures -> not equivalent,
+shown red.
+
+7.6 Migration: 'tool/migrate_region_syntax.py' rewrites the historical
+'||||' toggle framing to '##! potpourri' ... '####'. The legacy syntax is
+GONE (clean break): '||||' in input is ordinary content now. Note one
+tightening: the legacy toggle silently flushed a region left open at end
+of stream; the shebang framing makes that a loud error (7.1).
+
+
+8. VERDICTS AND THE DISPLAY
+===========================
+
+The element-level comparison verdict ('E_Verdict') carries five values:
+MISFIT (incomparable kinds), DIFFERENT, EQUIVALENT, and the two
+EQUIVALENT_*_VISIBLE_NOTHING variants (transparent token on one side).
+The VN variants are propagated, not collapsed, so downstream stages can
+account for noise without losing information; reduction to booleans
+happens only at the top ('semantics.is_equivalent_verdict', strict variant
+'is_plainly_equivalent_verdict' where a transparent token may not stand in
+for content).
+
+The Judge->Lawyer vocabulary mapping ('semantics.verdict_to_edit_id') is
+the single translation between verdicts and edit classes. The Lawyer's
+verdict reduction is code, not convention: 'LinePair.is_equivalent()'
+(insignificance neutralizes -> sequence-level edit class damns or clears ->
+cells decide) and 'ChunkPair.is_equivalent()' (chunk types agree where both
+sides exist; one-sided chunks are judged by their pairs).
+
+
+9. WHAT THE ENGINE DOES NOT DO
+==============================
+
+Stated explicitly, because each was considered and ruled out:
+
+  - NO cross-region or whole-file analogy solving. The global db is
+    sequential; regions are isolated. A "globally satisfiable" file whose
+    outer text contradicts its own established bindings is not equivalent.
+  - NO analogy leakage between regions and outer text, in either
+    direction.
+  - NO in-line visible-nothing collapse of separators (section 4).
+  - NO cost-threshold equivalence. Cost ranks; classes decide.
+
+
+10. STATEFUL CONSTRAINTS
+========================
+
+An element of the SEQUENTIAL outer text matching
+
+    (( <variable-name> : <number>|<quoted-string> ))
+
+is a CONSTRAINT BINDING: the variable enters the run's CONSTRAINT SPACE
+with the given value. Constraints live in the configuration as a plain
+dictionary, variable name -> expression (or list of expressions):
+
+    Configuration.constraint_db = {
+        "y": "y >= x",
+        "t": "t > 0 and t < 100",
+    }
+
+10.1 CHECK-ON-ENTRY. The moment a variable enters the space, ALL
+     constraints defined for it are checked against the CURRENT space.
+     Each input side (subject, nominal) has its OWN space; values develop
+     in line order. A variable without constraints of its own enters
+     freely -- it may serve as input to other constraints ('x' above).
+
+10.2 TEXTUAL EQUIVALENCE of two binding elements is decided by the NAME
+     alone; the VALUE is free. Whether a value is ACCEPTABLE is the
+     constraint space's judgment, not a textual one. Name mismatch =
+     DIFFERENT; kind mismatch (binding vs. plain text) = MISFIT.
+
+10.3 VERDICTS follow the malformed-data asymmetry (sections 7.5, D-21):
+       - SUBJECT-side violation -- constraint false, dependency not (yet)
+         in the space, division by zero, ANY evaluation failure -- makes
+         the test FAIL; the binding's cell is a MISMATCH (red). Never loud.
+       - NOMINAL-side violation is a BROKEN SPECIFICATION: the GOOD file
+         breaking its own law -> LOUD ConstraintSpecError. Within a pair
+         the nominal's bindings are processed FIRST (specification
+         validation precedes judgment).
+
+10.4 SEQUENTIALITY IS THE PRECONDITION. Bindings are active ONLY in the
+     sequential outer text. In order-free scopes "the value before" is
+     undefined by construction, so a NOMINAL binding there is a LOUD
+     RegionSyntaxError: potpourri, 'table unordered', 'table key'.
+     Scopes that never tolerance-lex are inert: verbatim, ignore, ordered
+     tables (a binding there is plain text). A subject-side binding in a
+     potpourri is a plain mismatch (kind MISFIT against any nominal line).
+
+10.5 REACHABILITY IS MIRRORED (THE LAW). Both faces process bindings in
+     the same line order and STOP at the first non-equivalent pair: the
+     Judge aborts; the Lawyer kills the space. Hence a loud nominal
+     violation behind a mismatch is raised by BOTH faces or by NEITHER.
+     Bindings on insignificant lines (blank/ignored) never enter: the
+     Judge's pipe drops those lines before it sees them.
+
+10.6 EXPRESSIONS are inspected as AST elements against a strict whitelist
+     (arithmetic, comparisons, boolean logic, the math function set,
+     string constants, Python string methods) and executed by Python with
+     empty builtins -- the same safety envelope as region parameter
+     expressions (D-22). Only PRESENT variables are bound at evaluation:
+     short-circuit logic ("y == 2 or y >= x") may pass without 'x'; a
+     missing variable raises exactly when actually needed (-> red).
+
+10.7 STATIC PRE-CHECKS are LOUD at ConstraintDb build time, before any
+     line is read: unparseable or non-whitelisted expressions, and the
+     CIRCULARITY test over the dependency graph (a cycle between
+     DIFFERENT variables; self-reference is natural and legal). A name
+     that is no known constraint variable is NOT a static error -- it is
+     a free input whose existence is a runtime question (10.6).
+
+     Implemented in engine/constraints.py; bindings lexed by
+     engine/input/pattern_finder.py (registered BEFORE the analogy
+     pattern -- same markers, more specific shape wins); faces wired in
+     region/line_sequence/{equivalence,associate}.py and main.py.
+     Verified by TEST/test-constraints.py and the 'constraints' family of
+     TEST/test-consistency-fuzz.py.
+
+

+D-22 (2026-07-18) POINT-CLOUD region (user-designed): coverage default =
+     nearest neighbour within 'limit' both ways (user ruling; 'limit',
+     not 'max_dist'); 'pair' = bijective; constraint = property over
+     BOTH streams; expressions carried in braces {...} (user ruling);
+     evaluated ONLY through the AST-whitelist evaluator; malformed-data
+     asymmetry per D-21's spirit (nominal loud, subject red).
+     [Stage 5; region/point_cloud/; section 7.5]
+
+D-23 (2026-07-18) Point-cloud fixed-radius queries accelerate via a
+     uniform grid (cell edge = limit; the query is fixed-radius, never
+     k-nearest -- a grid beats k-d/BVH here) for BUILT-IN metrics and
+     dimension <= 6; byte-identical to brute force (property-tested,
+     grid==brute 100/100; ~160x at N=3000). Expression metrics stay
+     brute BY PRINCIPLE: without a triangle inequality no structure can
+     prune correctly. [Stage 5b; region/point_cloud/spatial.py]

+     positionally / as a bag ('unordered') / by a key column; per-column

+     authoritative; malformed-data asymmetry (nominal loud, subject red).
+     One decision core feeds both faces. [Stage 6; region/table/;
+     section 7.5]
+
+D-25 (2026-07-18) POTPOURRI variants (user-requested): 'subset' (subject
+     is a subset of the nominal; surplus nominal lines legal, neutral) and
+     'duplicates' (LITERAL collapse by uniform string before matching;
+     collapsed repetitions neutral). Both nominal-authoritative, combine.
+     Threaded through the existing matcher via a VariantView, with
+     subset-aware count/availability/ultimates rules; plain-potpourri
+     behavior unchanged (all pre-existing goldens byte-identical).
+     [Stage 6; region/potpourri/variants.py; section 7.5]

+D-26 (2026-07-19) STATEFUL CONSTRAINTS (user-designed, complete ruling;
+     settles DISCUSSIONS/disc-stateful-constraints.txt): binding elements
+     '((name: number|"string"))' in the SEQUENTIAL outer text enter a
+     constraint space; check-on-entry against Configuration.constraint_db
+     (plain dictionary, name -> expression(s)); constraints may depend on
+     each other; subject-side violation / missing dependency / division
+     by zero / any evaluation failure = red cell mismatch (never loud);
+     nominal-side violation = loud (asymmetry); basic circularity test
+     precedes the run (loud); expressions are AST-inspected and executed
+     by Python (math + string functions, empty builtins); FORBIDDEN in
+     order-free scopes (potpourri, unordered/keyed tables: nominal loud).
+     Textual equivalence of bindings is by NAME; the value is judged by
+     the space. Reachability of loud errors is mirrored between the faces
+     by killing the space at the first non-equivalent pair. [Stage 7;
+     engine/constraints.py; section 10; TEST/test-constraints.py;
+     fuzz family 'constraints']
+
+
+D-27 (2026-08-09) NUMERIC TOLERANCE: POLE BAND, BOUNDED PRICE (user-ruled;
+     settles todo-19 and its two siblings found on location). The nominal
+     is the pole; the tolerance band is centred on it with radius
+     'abs(nominal) * ratio' -- a radius carries no sign (the missing
+     'abs()' made the band unsatisfiable for negative poles: the same
+     value in two spellings, '-100.0' vs '-100.00', compared unequal).
+     Both faces read the POLE's band: the Judge always did; the Lawyer's
+     substitution price subtracted the SUBJECT's epsilon and now subtracts
+     the nominal's -- one edit serves both, THE LAW keeps holding by
+     construction. The price of a substitution is a fraction of a full
+     substitution, bounded to [0, 1]: 'min(1, max(|s-n| - band, 0) /
+     max(|s|, |n|))'. Opposite-sign pairs previously priced up to ~2,
+     above INSERT+DELETE (= 2) and above the search's seeded per-pair
+     worst case (= 1, 'core/edit_operations/core.py:max_cost'), so the
+     cap restores both the edit-preference order and the pruning bound's
+     admissibility. Scale stays the pair's larger magnitude: the pole
+     defines the band, the pair defines the scale -- a pole-only scale
+     ('|n|') saturates every overshooting candidate at 1.0 and surrenders
+     candidate ranking to search order (GRAVEYARD). Golden impact: exactly
+     one file, 'reading/TEST/GOOD/test-line_element.py--LineElementNumber'
+     (a tolerated pair had priced as a difference: the golden recorded the
+     incoherence). [reading/line_element.py:LineElementNumber;
+     TEST/test-line_element.py choice 'NumberBand'; section 3]
+

+# Feature Reminder: Happy Constraints (Comparison Engine)
+
+## Background: happy patterns (already exist)
+
+The HWUT comparison engine already supports **happy patterns**: a pattern
+that, if it appears in *both* the nominal (known-good) and the actual
+output, makes the comparison succeed at that position regardless of which
+alternative matched on each side.
+
+    Happy pattern:   "hello|hallo|bonjour"
+    Effect:          nominal "hello" is equivalent to actual "bonjour"
+
+The alternatives are treated as interchangeable. A match on any branch in
+the nominal is equivalent to a match on any branch in the actual.
+
+
+## Proposed feature: happy constraints
+
+A **happy constraint** is a deliberate, computed extension of a happy
+pattern. Instead of a fixed set of interchangeable literals, equivalence
+at a text position is decided by *evaluating a predicate* over the value
+carried by that position.
+
+A constraint is **self-contained**: it constrains only the value of its own
+element. It cannot reference any other element's value. (Relating two values
+to each other is the test author's job, done in the test application's own
+code — not in the comparison engine.) This keeps a constraint a pure,
+stateless, per-element check, exactly like `NUMERIC` or `EQUIVALENCE_PATTERN`.
+
+### Text element form
+
+A text element subject to happy-constraint consideration has the form:
+
+    (<name>: <value>)
+
+Example occurrences in actual output:
+
+    (integration_steps: 212341)
+    (temperature: 37.4)
+    (label: "UPPER")
+
+### Value typing
+
+`<value>` is **either a number or a quoted string — nothing else.**
+
+- A numeric literal becomes `int` or `float` (Python literal form).
+- A quoted literal becomes `str`.
+- No bare words, no lists, no expressions, no other Python literals.
+
+This restriction is deliberate: because a value can only be a number or a
+quoted string, the closing `)` of the element is **never** ambiguous. A
+`)` inside a quoted string is part of the string; a `)` outside quotes ends
+the element. The lexer can therefore recognise `(<name>: <value>)` with a
+single, well-defined rule (see implementation hints). Parse the value with
+`ast.literal_eval` after isolating it, and reject anything that is not an
+`int`, `float`, or `str`.
+
+### Constraint definition
+
+Constraints are defined in the same section where happy patterns are
+defined, under a `HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS:` heading. Each constraint binds a
+`<name>` to a Python predicate over the single free variable `<name>`. The
+predicate must evaluate to a `bool`.
+
+    HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS: integration_steps: integration_steps % 2 == 1 and integration_steps < 30000
+    HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS: depth:             10 < depth < 500
+    HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS: label:             label[3] == "upper"
+
+The only name a predicate may reference is the `<name>` it is attached to.
+A predicate referencing any other name is a **definition-time error**.
+
+The mapping is `<name>` to predicate. If several conditions apply to one
+`<name>`, combine them in the one predicate with `and` (as in the
+`integration_steps` example) rather than across several definitions.
+
+
+## Evaluation semantics
+
+There is **no namespace and no rewrite.** When the comparison reaches a
+constraint element, it checks that element in place against the predicate
+registered for its `<name>`, and — if satisfied — continues. This mirrors
+how `LineElementNumber.compare()` decides equivalence locally.
+
+Given an actual-output element `(integration_steps: 212341)` and the
+definition:
+
+    HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS: integration_steps: integration_steps % 2 == 1 and integration_steps < 30000
+
+the engine, on reaching that position:
+
+1. Reads the element's name (`integration_steps`) and value (`212341`).
+2. Looks up the predicate registered for that name.
+3. Evaluates the predicate with its single variable bound to the value.
+4. Predicate holds  -> the position is **equivalent**; comparison continues.
+   Predicate fails  -> the position is **not equivalent**.
+
+In short: a constraint element is equivalent **iff its own value satisfies
+its own predicate**. Subject and nominal are compared position by position
+as today; the constraint replaces the literal text match at that one
+position with a predicate evaluation.
+
+### Name agreement between subject and nominal
+
+A constraint position pairs with the corresponding position on the other
+side. The two must carry the **same `<name>`**; differing names at paired
+positions is a normal `MISFIT`/`DIFFERENT`, just as differing tolerance
+types are today. The values need not be equal — each side's value must
+satisfy the predicate.
+
+### Marking a difference
+
+When a constraint is not satisfied, the diff marks the mismatch as:
+
+    actual:    (<name> NEQ <original value>)
+    nominal:   (<name>: <original value>)
+
+so the failing position is legible against the unchanged nominal form.
+
+### Refusing an invalid nominal
+
+A nominal output whose own constraint value violates the constraint must
+**not** be accepted by the HWUT engine. A nominal that cannot itself pass
+its predicate can never serve as a valid reference. This is a valid reason
+to throw an exception at parse time — an unacceptable nominal is rejected
+outright rather than silently producing a passing or failing comparison.
+
+
+## Parser: Python AST
+
+The predicate language **is** Python expression syntax. Each predicate is
+parsed with `ast.parse(expr, mode="eval")` and validated by walking the
+AST:
+
+- Only an allow-listed set of node types is accepted: comparisons, boolean
+  ops, the single bound `<name>`, literals, subscripts, arithmetic, and
+  calls to **built-in** functions only. No attribute access, no imports,
+  no arbitrary calls.
+- The only `Name` permitted is the constraint's own `<name>`. Any other
+  free name is a definition-time error (this is what enforces
+  "self-contained").
+- The expression must **evaluate to a `bool`**; this is checked on the
+  result at evaluation time, not statically.
+
+Helper functions are limited to Python's **built-ins**; no custom helper
+registry. For example `odd(...)` is not a built-in — write
+`integration_steps % 2 == 1` instead.
+
+Evaluation happens against a restricted namespace containing only the one
+bound variable (and the permitted built-ins).
+
+## Error handling
+
+Errors collapse onto the two outcomes already defined — there is no third
+"error" state surfaced to the user:
+
+- A **syntax error** or **execution error** (type error, failed built-in
+  call, non-boolean result) while evaluating against the **actual** output
+  translates directly to **not equivalent**.
+- The same failure while validating the **nominal** output translates to
+  **unacceptable as nominal**, i.e. the parse-time exception that rejects
+  the nominal.
+
+Note: predicate *syntax* errors and the *unknown-name* error are caught
+once at definition-compile time, so they surface before any comparison
+runs. Only value-dependent runtime errors can occur during comparison.
+
+
+## What this design deliberately avoids
+
+Dropping cross-references between constraint elements removes:
+
+- any **shared namespace** threaded through the comparison;
+- any dependence on **line order** ("which value was bound first");
+- any **potpourri special case** — because a self-contained predicate is
+  order-independent, it works identically inside a `||||` region and a
+  line sequence, with no CSP-style permutation search.
+
+A constraint is therefore a stateless, local, per-element tolerance.

+================================================================================
+IMPLEMENTATION GUIDE: Happy Constraints
+================================================================================
+Project: VUT / hwut -- compare component
+Scope:   Changes required to add the "happy constraint" tolerance.
+Status:  Design direction. Not final code. Verify every signature against the
+         live tree before editing.
+
+Companion: FEATURE-happy-constraints.md (the specification this realizes).
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+0. ONE-PARAGRAPH ORIENTATION
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+A happy constraint is a new per-element tolerance. A text element of the form
+"(name: value)" is lexed into a new LineElement subtype. Its equivalence is
+decided locally: the element's own value is fed to the predicate registered
+for "name"; predicate true => EQUIVALENT, false => DIFFERENT. The element is
+self-contained -- no other element's value is read -- so the change is
+stateless and lands entirely on the existing per-element compare() path. No
+analogy_db-style threading is introduced. No namespace object exists.
+
+The mental model is LineElementNumber: a number element holds a value and an
+epsilon and answers compare() by itself. A constraint element holds a value
+and a predicate and answers compare() by itself.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+1. DATA FLOW (mechanics)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+Text "(integration_steps: 212341)" travels:
+
+   configuration.py
+      HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS definitions ---> {name: compiled_predicate}
+                                              |
+                                              v
+   pattern_finder.py  (master regex gains a CONSTRAINT alternative;
+                       holds the {name: predicate} table)
+      line text ---> regex match ---> LineElement.from_match(CONSTRAINT,...)
+                                              |
+                                              v
+   line_element.py
+      LineElementConstraint(name, value, raw_value, predicate)
+         .compare(nominal_element):
+            same name?            no  -> MISFIT/DIFFERENT
+            self.value sat. pred? no  -> DIFFERENT
+            nominal.value sat.?   no  -> DIFFERENT   (defensive; see sec.7)
+            otherwise                 -> EQUIVALENT, None   (no analogy)
+                                              |
+                                              v
+   engine/line.py __compare_core()  (unchanged: walks elements, calls compare())
+                                              |
+                                              v
+   equivalence_check/line.py, equivalence_check/potpourri.py  (UNCHANGED)
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+2. NEW TOLERANCE ID  (engine/enums.py)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+Add one member to E_ToleranceId:
+
+      CONSTRAINT = 7
+
+E_ToleranceId is (int, Enum); next free value is 7. No other enum touched.
+structural_hash() in line_element.py treats CONSTRAINT as a variable element
+(type only, no content) -- it already does this for everything that is not
+STRING, so no change there.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+3. PREDICATE COMPILER  (new file: engine/happy_constraint.py)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+Owns parsing + validation + evaluation of one predicate. Stateless.
+
+API:
+
+   compile_predicate(name: str, expr: str) -> Predicate
+      """RETURN: Predicate, a validated callable for one constraint.
+
+      Raises HappyConstraintError on syntax error, on a disallowed AST node,
+      or on any free name other than 'name'.
+
+      Parses 'expr' (mode="eval"), walks the AST against the allow-list,
+      verifies the only Name used is 'name', and wraps a compiled code object
+      so it can be evaluated against a one-entry namespace.
+      """
+
+   Predicate.holds(value) -> bool
+      """RETURN: True,  value satisfies the predicate.
+                 False, it does not, OR evaluation raised, OR result not bool.
+
+      Binds the constraint's single variable to 'value' and evaluates. Any
+      exception or non-bool result yields False (see error policy, sec.7).
+      """
+
+   class HappyConstraintError(Exception)
+      """Raised for malformed/illegal predicate definitions, and reused for
+      'nominal violates its own constraint' (sec.6)."""
+
+ALLOW-LIST (ast node types):
+   Expression, BoolOp(And,Or), UnaryOp(Not,USub,UAdd), BinOp(Add,Sub,Mult,
+   Div,FloorDiv,Mod,Pow), Compare(Lt,LtE,Gt,GtE,Eq,NotEq), Name(Load only),
+   Constant, Subscript, Slice, Call.
+   Call.func MUST be a bare Name in _SAFE_BUILTINS (no Attribute -> blocks
+   "().__class__..." and os.system style escapes).
+
+_SAFE_BUILTINS (decide final set; suggested):
+   len, abs, min, max, int, float, str, round, ord, all, any
+   ('odd' is NOT here -> use "x % 2 == 1"; Mod is allow-listed.)
+
+EVAL SANDBOX:
+   eval(code, {"__builtins__": {}}, {name: value, **_SAFE_BUILTINS})
+   -- empty real builtins; only the curated names reachable.
+
+bool-ness: checked on the RESULT inside .holds():  isinstance(r, bool) and r.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+4. CONFIGURATION  (configuration.py)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ConfigurationPatternFinder gains:
+
+      constraint_f:            bool = False
+      happy_constraint_list:   list = field(default_factory=list)
+         # raw "name: expr" strings as written under HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS:
+
+The "name: expr" splitting happens where HAPPY-CONSTRAINTS lines are read
+(same reader that fills equivalent_pattern_list). Split on the FIRST ':'
+only -- the name is left of it, the predicate text is everything to the right
+(predicates contain ':' only inside string literals, never structurally; but
+splitting on first ':' and trusting the name to be an identifier is safe).
+
+No compilation in configuration.py -- raw strings only. Compilation is the
+PatternFinder's job (sec.5) so a malformed predicate fails at finder setup,
+i.e. once, early, with the offending line in hand.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+5. LEXER  (input/pattern_finder.py)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+5.1 SETUP (__init__)
+   When config.constraint_f and config.happy_constraint_list:
+     a) Build the predicate table:
+           self._constraint_table = {
+               name: happy_constraint.compile_predicate(name, expr)
+               for (name, expr) in parsed_definitions
+           }
+        compile_predicate may raise HappyConstraintError here -> surfaces at
+        finder construction (acceptable, early, deterministic).
+     b) Register ONE master-regex alternative for the element shape:
+
+           NAME  = r"[A-Za-z_]\w*"
+           STR   = r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"' + r"|'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'"
+           NUM   = r"-?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?"
+           VALUE = f"(?:{STR}|{NUM})"
+           CONSTRAINT_RE = rf"\(\s*{NAME}\s*:\s*{VALUE}\s*\)"
+
+        Register via the existing _register() so it joins the master regex
+        and gets a Gn group + TolerancePattern(CONSTRAINT, ...). Use named
+        SUBGROUPS for name and value, OR re-match a small dedicated regex on
+        m.group() in do() to split name/value (named subgroups inside the
+        master alternation are simpler; verify the regex module allows the
+        duplicate-group-name situation across alternatives -- if not, split
+        by re-matching in do()).
+
+   ORDERING: register CONSTRAINT before NUMERIC. A bare "212341" must not be
+   eaten by NUMERIC when it sits inside "(name: 212341)". Because the
+   constraint alternative consumes the whole "(...)" span including the
+   number, finditer's left-to-right longest-at-position behavior keeps them
+   apart -- but place CONSTRAINT early in re_parts to be safe and document it.
+
+5.2 do()  -- emit the element
+   In the match loop, when tolerance.id is CONSTRAINT:
+     - extract name_str and raw_value_str (named groups or re-match)
+     - look up predicate = self._constraint_table.get(name_str)
+         predicate is None  -> the element names an UNDECLARED constraint.
+                               Treat as plain text: append LineElementString(
+                               m.group()) and continue. (A "(x: 5)" with no
+                               declared constraint is just literal text.)
+     - else build the element:
+           LineElement.from_match(CONSTRAINT, m.group(),
+                                  self.numeric_tolerance_ratio,
+                                  constraint=(name_str, raw_value_str, predicate))
+   DO NOT route CONSTRAINT through _get_matching_pattern_indices (that cache
+   and the pattern_i_set argument are EQUIVALENCE_PATTERN-only).
+
+   from_match signature: add an optional keyword (e.g. constraint=None) rather
+   than overloading pattern_i_set. Keep the hot NUMERIC/EQUIVALENCE paths
+   untouched.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+6. LINE ELEMENT  (input/line_element.py)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+New subtype. Model on LineElementNumber (value carried, local compare()).
+
+   class LineElementConstraint(LineElement):
+       __slots__ = ('name', 'value', 'raw_value', '_predicate')
+
+       def __init__(self, name, raw_value, predicate):
+           LineElement.__init__(self, E_ToleranceId.CONSTRAINT, raw_value)
+           self.name       = name
+           self.raw_value  = raw_value
+           self.value      = _literal(raw_value)   # ast.literal_eval; int/float/str only
+           self._predicate = predicate
+
+       def compare(self, nominal):
+           """RETURN: [0] MISFIT,     nominal is not a constraint element
+                          DIFFERENT,  same kind but name differs OR a value
+                                      fails the predicate
+                          EQUIVALENT, names agree and both values satisfy
+                      [1] None, no analogy is ever produced
+           """
+           if nominal.tolerance_id == E_ToleranceId.VISIBLE_NOTHING:
+               return E_Verdict.EQUIVALENT_NOMINAL_VISIBLE_NOTHING, None
+           if self.tolerance_id != nominal.tolerance_id:
+               return E_Verdict.MISFIT, None
+           if self.name != nominal.name:
+               return E_Verdict.DIFFERENT, None
+           if not self._predicate.holds(self.value):
+               return E_Verdict.DIFFERENT, None
+           if not nominal._predicate.holds(nominal.value):
+               return E_Verdict.DIFFERENT, None        # see sec.7 note
+           return E_Verdict.EQUIVALENT, None
+
+       def edit_distance_relative(self, nominal):
+           # 0 when equivalent, else fall back to string distance for display cost
+           v, _ = self.compare(nominal)
+           return 0 if E_Verdict.is_equivalent(v) else \
+                  LineElement.edit_distance_relative(self, nominal)
+
+   from_match(): add  case E_ToleranceId.CONSTRAINT:
+                          name, raw, pred = constraint
+                          return LineElementConstraint(name, raw, pred)
+
+   _literal(raw): ast.literal_eval(raw); assert type in (int, float, str);
+                  on failure raise HappyConstraintError (malformed value text).
+
+   __hash__: like LineElementNumber, DO NOT override -- equivalence is
+   predicate-derived, not content-identity. structural_hash already keys
+   CONSTRAINT on type only.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+7. ERROR / VERDICT POLICY  (the two-outcome rule)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+Predicate.holds() swallows runtime errors -> False. So during comparison a
+constraint can only resolve to satisfied / not-satisfied; never an exception
+escaping into the engine. This realizes "execution error on actual ==
+not equivalent".
+
+NOMINAL VALIDATION (the parse-time refusal):
+   A nominal element whose OWN value fails its predicate must abort the run.
+   Two equivalent placement options:
+
+   (a) At lex time, when constraint_f is set AND the finder is lexing the
+       nominal stream: after building LineElementConstraint, if
+       predicate.holds(value) is False -> raise HappyConstraintError.
+       Requires the finder to know it is lexing nominal vs subject.
+
+   (b) Symmetric, engine-side: the "nominal._predicate.holds(...)" line in
+       compare() (sec.6) returns DIFFERENT for a bad nominal. To make it FATAL
+       rather than a silent mismatch, the nominal-side check is better done
+       once up front (option a), and the compare()-time nominal check can then
+       be dropped as redundant.
+
+   RECOMMENDATION: do option (a). It gives the exact "unacceptable as nominal"
+   exception, keeps compare() to a single value test (self only), and matches
+   the spec's "rejected at parse time". The nominal-side test inside compare()
+   (sec.6) then becomes unnecessary -- remove it once (a) is in place.
+
+   Which stream is nominal? The two EquivalenceCheckChunkPipe / Line instances
+   are built separately in main.py (subject vs nominal). Thread a boolean
+   "nominal_f" from the pipe into PatternFinder.do(), or give the finder a
+   "raise_on_constraint_violation" flag set only for the nominal finder. Keep
+   it off the hot path: a single attribute check.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+8. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE  (important -- guards against over-engineering)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+   main.py                         : UNCHANGED. No namespace, no new threaded
+                                     return value, no context-local registry.
+   analogy_db.py / frozen_analogy_db: UNCHANGED. Constraints never emit an
+                                     analogy (compare() returns None for [1]).
+   engine/line.py __compare_core   : UNCHANGED. It already zips sequence_v and
+                                     calls element.compare(); a constraint
+                                     element answers like any other.
+   equivalence_check/line.py       : UNCHANGED.
+   equivalence_check/potpourri.py  : UNCHANGED. Self-contained predicates are
+                                     order-independent, so potpourri pairing
+                                     and the CSP/bipartite matching need no
+                                     awareness of constraints -- a constraint
+                                     element compares locally inside whatever
+                                     pairing the solver proposes.
+   input_chunk.py / chunk_pipe.py  : UNCHANGED (lines still flow through the
+                                     PatternFinder; the new element rides along).
+   input_chunk_zip.py              : UNCHANGED.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+9. UI / PROTOCOL  (feeder/ui.py)  -- only if constraint cells are displayed
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+   - ConfigInst: add constraint_f if the receiver needs to know constraints
+     are active (mirrors the existing flag-mirroring block in feed()).
+   - tolerance_id flows through cells already; CONSTRAINT passes through
+     bake_line_pair_inst like NUMERIC (no analogy provenance to bake).
+   - Adding any field to a protocol dataclass changes _get_protocol_hash(),
+     so the receiver's SIGNATURE check will flag a version bump. Expected.
+     Regenerate SIGNATURE_UI_PROTOCOL.txt (python ui.py -w).
+   - The diff rendering "(name NEQ value)" vs "(name: value)" is a RECEIVER
+     concern: the engine emits a non-equivalent constraint cell carrying name
+     + raw_value; the display layer formats the NEQ form. Do not bake the NEQ
+     string into the engine.
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+10. RATIONALE LEDGER  (why, separated from the mechanics above)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+   * Self-contained constraints (no cross-reference):
+       PROBLEM:  cross-element references make equivalence depend on binding
+                 order; inside a potpourri (order irrelevant) this becomes a
+                 constraint-satisfaction search over line permutations.
+       COST of avoiding: a test author wanting two values related must compute
+                 the relation in the application and emit a single derived
+                 value/flag. Near-zero practical loss.
+       PAYOFF:   constraint = stateless local tolerance; ZERO changes to
+                 main.py, analogy_db, the equivalence-check layer, and the
+                 potpourri solver (sec.8).
+
+   * Modeling on LineElementNumber rather than LineElementAnalogy:
+       Analogy carries cross-line state (the analogy_db) and returns an
+       analogy pair from compare(). A constraint carries none and returns
+       None. Number is the right structural twin: local value + local verdict.
+
+   * Built-ins only, predicate must return bool:
+       COST:    no domain helpers (odd/even); author rewrites as arithmetic.
+       PAYOFF:  no helper registry to maintain or secure; the AST allow-list
+                plus empty __builtins__ is the entire sandbox surface.
+
+   * Nominal validation up front (option a, sec.7):
+       A reference output that cannot satisfy its own predicate is meaningless
+       as a reference. Failing fast at lex time gives a precise error and lets
+       compare() stay single-sided.
+
+   * INVARIANTS future changes must not break:
+       - compare() for a constraint reads ONLY self (and, transitionally,
+         nominal for the to-be-removed nominal check); never any other element.
+       - A constraint NEVER produces an analogy.
+       - Predicate evaluation NEVER raises into the engine (holds() traps).
+       - Removing constraint_f / happy_constraint_list returns the engine to
+         byte-identical prior behavior (CONSTRAINT alternative absent from the
+         master regex; from_match never sees the id).
+
+
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+11. OPEN DECISIONS
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+   * Final _SAFE_BUILTINS set (sec.3).
+   * Undeclared "(x: 5)" in output: treated as plain text (sec.5.2). Confirm
+     this is desired vs. an error.
+   * Quote style for string values: allow both ' and " (regex in 5.1 does),
+     or restrict to one.
+   * Whether display ever needs constraint cells (sec.9) or the feature is
+     equivalence-only for now.
